key_insight: An NLP pipeline using radiology report text can identify brain metastases at scale, including cases missed by registry-only capture.
clinical_relevance: This could improve population-level surveillance of brain metastases and support more complete cancer registry workflows across provinces.
method: Trained two Bio_ClinicalBERT models on the Findings and Impressions sections of brain/head radiology reports
Combined both section outputs by taking the maximum predicted probability as the report-level prediction
Validated internally and externally using manually labeled reports from Alberta, Ontario, and British Columbia
evidence_signal: The model was trained on 1,879 samples and tested on 1,833 internal validation reports, achieving sensitivity 0.888 at a 0.4 threshold and showing external sensitivity of 0.918 in Ontario and 0.726 in British Columbia.
watch_item: Performance varied across provinces, so deployment will need local validation, threshold tuning, and workflow integration to avoid missed cases or false positives.
paper_title: Natural Language Processing Based Solution for Labeling Brain Metastasis Identified in Radiology Reports
